name: Robust multilevel quantum-control pulses
description: pulse(target_gate, hardware_model) -> (80,2) IQ amplitudes rad/ns for 40 ns X-pi gate in a three-level Duffing transmon. Enforce amplitude .4 rad/ns and slew .12 rad/ns/ns including endpoints. Independent Lindblad expm and refined DOP853 evaluate six Bloch states over 3x3 detuning/calibration cases, relaxation and dephasing. Score mean plus worst average gate infidelity; report leakage. Explicit simulation, not QuOCS benchmark reproduction.

papers.title: Simple pulses for elimination of leakage in weakly nonlinear qubits
papers.task_relation: The local task optimizes a fixed-duration IQ pulse in an explicit three-level Duffing/Lindblad model with detuning and calibration uncertainty. Its ensemble, pulse discretization, bounds, and loss are local choices, not a reproduction of the paper's experimental performance.
papers.primary_goal: Construct control pulses that suppress leakage and enable accurate fast gates in weakly nonlinear qubits.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Implement fast, accurate gates in weakly anharmonic superconducting qubits while suppressing leakage.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Leakage suppression during physical qubit control is the paper's central quantum-device problem.
science_relevance.reason: The cited work solves a concrete control error mechanism, so a generic optimal-control toolkit citation is unnecessary.
